name: Dichanthelium

project_scope.selection_mode: existing-species genus FINISH/ENRICH; no new admissions
project_scope.native_range_status: preserved as prior species records; NOT reaudited
project_scope.note: These four are the installed canonical project concepts, NOT a comprehensive county-native Dichanthelium checklist.

look_here_first: DICHANTHELIUM rosette-grasses: the spring flowering head and late-season leafy branches may look like different plants. Begin with an actual rooted winter/spring ROSETTE and LEAF BASE, inspect a true hair-fringe LIGULE at the separated blade–sheath collar, and measure several mature oval SPIKELETS. Open panicles overlap among all four installed taxa. Existing photographs show 1 FLOWER MACRO, 1 mixed-grass HABIT view and 2 OPEN PANICLE details; do not label anatomy outside each photo.

recognition.where_to_look_first: 1) Spring basal rosette and autumn leafy secondary shoots → 2) blade base & width → 3) true collar hair fringe under 10–20× → 4) 3 calibrated mature spikelets → 5) complete flowering head. Existing photos do not show the diagnostic ligules.
priority: Identify whether photographed record is a flower macro, whole grass habitat, or open head; none of these alone gives all species characters
Do not equate a spring open head with an autumn fascicled branching specimen unless same rooted plant is documented
D. lindheimeri tiny blunt ~1.3–1.6 mm spikelets and conspicuous hair ligule; old synonym D. acuminatum var. lindheimeri is not a duplicate
D. commutatum broadly lance/cordate stem blade bases, minute/absent true ligule and ~2.1–3.2 mm spikelets
D. oligosanthes broad winter rosette, ~2.9–4 mm spikelets and generally longer ~1–4 mm collar fringe
D. pedicellatum slender ~1.3–5.5 mm spring leaves, exceptionally short ~0.25–0.5 mm true hair ligule and ~3–3.5 mm spikelets
D. oligosanthes and D. pedicellatum spikelet sizes overlap. No macro/ruler or rosette means tentative Dichanthelium sp.
recognition.photo_guardrail: One source-labelled image is a mixed grass scene, and the flower macro exposes only reproduction. No photographed size, ligule, actual rosette or native Hays voucher proven.

comparison_lesson.title: Four rosette panicgrasses: learn different photo roles and actual measurable characters
comparison_lesson.memory_rule: COMMUTATUM broad/cordate blade + tiny ligule; LINDHEIMERI tiny 1.3–1.6 mm spikelet + long collar hair; OLIGOSANTHES broad rosette + large 2.9–4 mm spikelets; PEDICELLATUM skinny blades + very short 0.25–0.5 mm ligule.
quick_split: VARIABLE PANICGRASS: first find the broad, often somewhat heart-based stem leaves and true short or absent hair ligule on a rooted shoot. Existing reproductive photo is GREAT for SEEING anthers, feathery red stigmas and a hairy spikelet, but cannot prove the leaf base, size, or species. Confirm a mature 2.1–3.2 mm spikelet and leaf-base/collar before calling D. commutatum.

LINDHEIMER'S PANICGRASS: the best species clue is the remarkably TINY, blunt-obovoid ripe spikelets (~1.3–1.6 mm), together with prominent hair-fringe ligule and long basal blade-margin cilia on otherwise often smooth yellow-green leaves. The ONLY current archived photo is a dense grass scene—not a measured spikelet or species-diagnostic close-up. Record source ID provisional until same-plant macro exists. Avoid duplicate D. acuminatum var. lindheimeri cards.

FEW-FLOWERED PANICGRASS: recognize the rather OPEN spring flowering panicle and many separate small oval spikelets, then locate the broader winter basal ROSETTE on the same rooted clump and measure ripe spikelets (~2.9–4 mm). Existing photo really shows panicle and oval units, NOT size/ligule. A hair-fringe ligule usually longer than tiny pedicellatum's ~0.25–0.5 mm must be photographed under scale.

CEDAR ROSETTE GRASS: first find NARROW, thin spring blades (roughly 1.3–5.5 mm wide), then inspect a VERY SHORT fringe of ligule hairs (~0.25–0.5 mm). Ripe spikelets are about 3–3.5 mm and overlap D. oligosanthes. Source photo shows separate oval spikelets on threadlike stems, but neither measurable size nor tiny collar curtain. Leave provisional until same plant leaves and glumes are available.
guardrails: Never assume the 4 images show 4 confirmed distinguishing head silhouettes; commutatum photo is flowering stamens/stigmas, lindheimeri photo is mixed vegetation only, oligosanthes and pedicellatum show different open panicles.
Exact mm numbers in the botanical descriptions are from source material, not measured from current photographs. Glumes and collars need actual photographed mm scale.
A true grass LIGULE is at the blade–sheath collar; do not mistake basal blade margin cilia or nearby sheath hairs for a ligule.
D. oligosanthes and D. pedicellatum mature spikelets frequently overlap; use leaf blade width and ligule length together.
D. acuminatum var. lindheimeri taxonomic synonym is an existing concept, not an uninstalled extra species.
Species photo determinations and county native-range status remain as historically stored; no BONAP/NAPA recertification.

what_to_teach_crew: The genus looks very different in spring versus autumn: document rosette, flowering head and late secondary shoots on the same rooted plant.
Identify photo ROLE first: commutatum photo is excellent for anthers/stigmas, lindheimeri is landscape-scale, oligosanthes and pedicellatum are inflorescence cues.
Panicle openness is shared. Species must be decided by measured spikelet size, true collar hair fringe, stem-blade width/base and appropriate whole plant.
Commutatum: examine broad sometimes cordate stem leaves and minute/absent true ligule; its flowering photo alone does not show either.
Lindheimeri: seek genuinely tiny 1.3–1.6 mm mature spikelets and long collar hairs; no such details are currently visible in its archive.
Oligosanthes versus pedicellatum: spikelet lengths overlap; pedicellatum has narrower leaves and very short ~0.25–0.5 mm ligule, oligosanthes usually longer ~1–4 mm.
Do not treat the D. acuminatum var. lindheimeri historical concept as a fifth installed card. Document uncertainty instead of assigning a false species label.
visual_needs: For all four: exact same plant ROOTED spring rosette, early open inflorescence, late leafy autumn fascicles and close leaf base with a ruler.
For D. commutatum: true broad/cordate blade base, close true collar fringe; flower/anther/stigma image is already usable.
For D. lindheimeri: replace/add a close isolated flowering plant, 1.3–1.6 mm mature blunt spikelet beside 1-mm scale, hairy collar versus leaf-base cilia.
For D. oligosanthes: winter rosette, measured large 2.9–4 mm spikelet, 1–4.2 mm hair-fringe ligule.
For D. pedicellatum: very thin vernal leaf width, exceptionally short 0.25–0.5 mm ligule and measured 3–3.5 mm ripe spikelet.
Do not annotate glume veins/hairs, tubercle bases, ligules or season-matched roots on current photo pixels: they are not resolvable.
